title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the sequel of 'La Longue Marche', in the part on the 'équation des lacets'. The main objects are:
- the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} (M_{0,3}), with loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ around the punctures;
- a profinite 'Teichmüller/quantization' group Ŝ_{0,3}, extended by the orientation-reversing involution τ_∞. It contains the order-3 rotation ρ (permuting 0→1→∞) and τ'_∞ = σ_∞τ_∞.
- an automorphism φ̂ (a Galois or GT-type element), and elements u_λ in the normaliser of L_0 that commute with φ̂.

The commutation condition is relation (5) with λ=1. On the previous page Grothendieck notes that (5) is tautological for x=l_0. It therefore suffices to impose it at x=l_1 (giving his condition (1D)) or at x=l_∞. He also proves (4∞): τ'_∞(ρ)=ρ^{-1}.

On this page:
1. Suppose u(ρ)=ρ^μ (41). Since ρ has order 3 and u is an automorphism, μ must be a unit mod 3, so μ ≡ ±1 (mod 3).
2. Define α_3(μ) ∈ Z/2 by μ ≡ (-1)^{α_3} (mod 3) (42). Using (4∞), this gives u(ρ) = τ'_∞^{α_3}(ρ) (43).
3. Evaluate (5) at x=l_∞, using u(l_∞) = int(f_∞^{-1}) l_∞^μ and φ̂(l_∞) = ρ^{-1}:
   - φ̂u(l_∞) = int(φ̂(f_∞^{-1})) ρ^{-μ};
   - uφ̂(l_∞) = u(ρ^{-1}) = int(α)(ρ^{-1}).
   Equating gives int(φ̂(f_∞)α)(ρ) = ρ^μ.
4. Combining with (43) gives (44): the element τ'_∞^{α_3} φ̂(f_∞) α of Ŝ_{0,3} = Ŝ^+_{0,3}·{1,τ_∞} centralises ρ.

On the next page Grothendieck invokes a principle he says is not fully established in the profinite setting: the centraliser of ρ is ⟨ρ⟩. This turns (44) into an equation τ'^{α_3} φ̂(f_∞) α = ρ^j. He then makes it explicit using f_∞^{-1} = ρ^{-1}(ξ^{-1}), with ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}.

What it serves: this is Grothendieck's own derivation of the order-3 ('cycle'/hexagon-type) relation for automorphisms of the profinite π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points. It includes the orientation-reversing component through the parity α_3.
errors: The step u(ρ^{-1}) = int(α)(ρ^{-1}) sits uneasily with (41), u(ρ)=ρ^μ, unless u on Ŝ is implicitly of the form int(α)∘(something). The notation leaves the precise nature of u and α ambiguous.

Passing from int(...)ρ = ρ^μ = int(τ'^{α_3})ρ to (44) needs int(τ'^{-α_3}·...). Writing τ'^{α_3} is harmless only if τ'_∞ is an involution, or at least τ'^2 centralises ρ. This is assumed but not stated.
The next page relies on 'centraliser of ρ = ⟨ρ⟩' in the profinite group. Grothendieck himself says this is not established in the profinite setting, so the argument is conditional there.

ideas.what: Derivation of the 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation for automorphisms of π̂_1(P^1-{0,1,∞}) commuting with the rotation ρ, by evaluating the commutation condition at the loop l_∞.
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon / order-3 relation in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group (GT-hat)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and the role of the M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} level; it does not contain this computation.

ideas.what: Parity α_3(μ) ∈ Z/2 defined by μ ≡ (-1)^{α_3} mod 3, used to incorporate the orientation-reversing involution τ'_∞ acting on ρ by inversion.
ideas.modern_name: Extended (real/orientation-reversing) GT, i.e. GT with complex conjugation; the mod-3 reduction of the cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Treatments of GT with complex conjugation in the later literature (e.g. Lochak–Schneps school); exact attribution unsure

ideas.what: Reduction to a centraliser condition: an element of Ŝ_{0,3} must centralise ρ; the centraliser is then assumed to be ⟨ρ⟩.
ideas.modern_name: Centralisers of torsion elements in profinite mapping class / braid groups

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine step in Grothendieck's private rederivation of GT-type relations, with an orientation-reversing component included. The resulting relations are well known since Drinfeld and Ihara. The only minor point of interest is his explicit tracking of the Z/2 parity α_3 via τ'_∞, but analogous extended-GT treatments exist.
transcription_corrections: Line (41): the 'μ ∈ Z/3Z' is probably 'μ ∈ Z/3Z convenable' read as an exponent class mod 3. The original may intend μ in Ẑ^* reduced mod 3.
The crossed-out remark after (43) reads roughly 'qui équivaut à ρ^μ = τ'^{α_3}_∞(ρ)', i.e. it is not a separate formula.
The superscript annotation reads 'α_3 = α_3(μ)' attached to τ'_∞ in the line ρ^μ = τ'^{α_3}_∞(ρ) ≝ int(τ'^{α_3}_∞)(ρ).
In the margin before ρ^μ there is a stray 'φ', probably the start of a crossed-out symbol.
